name: Obsidian-Cathedral
specific_features: Enormous obsidian spires formed by rapid cooling events
Thermophilic microbial mats in cooling lava channels
description: Obsidian-Cathedral is a small volcanic world dominated by towering spires of volcanic glass that rise from plains of black basalt like the buttresses of some infernal place of worship. The low gravity allows lava fountains to reach extraordinary heights before cooling, creating delicate glass structures that would collapse under heavier gravitational pull. Active shield volcanoes dot the surface, their broad flanks glowing with rivers of molten rock that carve ever-changing channels across the landscape.

The toxic atmosphere is a choking mixture of sulfur dioxide, carbon dioxide, and volcanic particulates that reduce visibility to mere meters during eruption events. Heat radiates from every surface, the ground itself too hot to touch in most regions, while the obsidian spires crack and sing as thermal stress cycles them between expansion and contraction. The beauty here is lethal, every gleaming surface a reminder that this world was not made for human presence.

Despite the hellish conditions, extremophilic microorganisms have colonized the cooling margins of lava flows, forming thick mats of heat-resistant biofilms that metabolize sulfur compounds. These organisms represent some of the most thermally tolerant life ever documented, surviving temperatures that would sterilize most known ecosystems. Their discovery has prompted intense study into the upper limits of biological heat tolerance and the possibility that life could persist on worlds previously dismissed as too hostile.

Mining operations on Obsidian-Cathedral focus on the rare earth elements concentrated in volcanic deposits, materials critical for advanced electronics and starship components. The low gravity makes extraction physically manageable but complicates logistics, as equipment designed for standard gravity behaves unpredictably. Every operation is a race against the next eruption cycle, and the planet has already claimed three automated mining rigs to unexpected lava surges that arrived faster than predictive models anticipated.
